contract.proves:
Verify that cluster-doctor reports no ERROR-severity findings against a
settled cluster.

Why this scenario exists:

On 2026-08-11 the certification suite scored 34/36 green while
cluster-doctor simultaneously reported 39 findings, 20 of them ERROR — a
corrupted etcd member on node-2, a poisoned scylladb package digest, and
nine units wedged in start-pre behind a failed ScyllaDB. Every one of those
defects was real, and the scenario suite sailed past all of them, because
the suite asserts almost entirely on PRESENCE (is the service registered? is
the unit active?) while the doctor asserts on COHERENCE ACROSS LAYERS (does
installed state match the manifest? does runtime match installed?).

A green suite alongside a 20-ERROR doctor report means the suite was not
measuring the thing that was broken. This scenario closes that gap by making
the doctor's own verdict a gated assertion instead of something a human has
to remember to read.

What it asserts, and what it deliberately does not:

- ERROR/CRITICAL count MUST be zero. These are coherence violations with an
  identified owner and a remediation; none should survive a settled cluster.
- WARN is recorded as evidence but NOT gated. The quickstart runs MinIO in
  standalone mode across 5 nodes, which is a legitimate standing WARN for
  this topology (objectstore.standalone_in_cluster). Gating on zero WARN
  would make the scenario permanently red for a known, accepted condition,
  and a permanently red test is one people learn to ignore.
- reduced_harvest MUST be false. When collector sub-fetches fail, the doctor
  marks its findings "[reduced-harvest]" and its verdict is bounded by
  partial data. A zero-ERROR count harvested from partial data is absence of
  evidence, not evidence of health — accepting it would rebuild the exact
  false-green this scenario exists to prevent
  (ops.always.doctor.reduced-harvest-honesty).
- reachable MUST be true. An unreachable doctor is not a clean cluster; it
  is an unknown one. Without this the probe's zero counts on a dead RPC
  would read as perfect health.

Run placement: functional, not resilience. The doctor legitimately reports
ERRORs while chaos is in flight (a stopped node IS unconverged), so this
belongs in a suite that runs against a settled cluster.
